paper.title: Adaptive Experimentation When You Can't Experiment

settings.name_in_paper: CPET-LB with known structural model Gamma
unmapped: Confounded (endogenous) noise: learner picks instrument z_t, observes x_t = Gamma^T z_t + eta_t and y_t = x_t^T theta + eps_t with eta and eps correlated; instrumental-variable exclusion restriction E[z_t eps_t]=0
Transductive: measurement set Z differs from evaluation set W; goal is argmax_{w in W} w^T theta
eps_t 1-sub-Gaussian, eta_t sigma_eta^2-sub-Gaussian vector; Gamma invertible
The learner knows an upper bound L_nu on the sub-Gaussian parameter of nu = eta^T theta + eps

settings.name_in_paper: CPET-LB with fully unknown structural model
unmapped: Confounded (endogenous) noise with instrumental variables; learner observes x_t and y_t
Transductive: measurement set Z differs from evaluation set W
Gamma unknown and must be estimated
The learner knows upper bounds L_nu >= sigma_nu^2 and L_eta >= sigma_eta^2 and a lower bound gamma_min on lambda_min(Gamma)
The stopping rule of the Gamma-estimator uses ||theta||_2, so the learner knows the norm of theta (recorded as S)
settings.definition_quote: We now consider the setting where Gamma is fully unknown. The difficulty of this setting is that the data collection process needs to support both estimation of Gamma and theta simultaneously.

settings.name_in_paper: CPET-LB non-adaptive oracle lower bound (lower bound)
unmapped: Confounded noise: [eta, eps] jointly Gaussian N(0, Sigma) with arbitrary correlation matrix Sigma
settings.definition_quote: Consider a problem instance characterized by $\mathcal{W}\subset \mathbb{R}^d, \mathcal{Z}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $\Gamma \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Assume $\Gamma$ is known, $\theta$ is unknown, and the noise process is jointly Gaussian and defined by $\gamma := \begin{bmatrix}\eta & \epsilon \end{bmatrix}\sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)$ where $\Sigma\in \mathbb{R}^{(d+1)\times (d+1)}$ is an arbitrary correlation matrix. For $\delta \in (0, 0.05]$, if the non-adaptive oracle algorithm acquires $T\leq \sigma^2\rho^{\ast}\log(1/\delta)/2$ samples on the problem instance where $\sigma^2:=v^{\top}\Sigma v$ and $v:=\begin{bmatrix}\theta & 1\end{bmatrix}\in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, then $\mathbb{P}(\widehat{w}\neq w^{\ast})\geq \delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: CPET-LB with Gamma-hat estimated from offline data

parameters.n_offline: T_off offline samples for estimating Gamma

unmapped: Learner is given an OLS estimate of Gamma from an offline non-adaptive dataset of size T_off collected via design xi
The learner knows L_nu, L_eta and uses ||theta||_2 in gamma
Returns a 6*gamma-good arm where gamma depends on offline estimation error

source.label: thm:complexity knownGamma
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg-TrueGamma} is $\delta$-PAC and terminates in at most $c(1+\omega)L_\nu\rho^{\ast}\log(1/\delta)+cr(\omega)$ samples, where $c$ hides logarithmic factors of $\Delta:=\min_w\langle w^{\ast}-w, \theta\rangle$ and $\abr{\mc{W}}$, as well as constants.

results.notes: delta-PAC; sample complexity holds on the good event (prob >= 1-delta). c hides logs of Delta and |W|, hence O_tilde.

symbols.rho_0: max_{w != w*} ||w*-w||^2 under the E-optimal design A(lambda_E,Gamma)^{-1}

source.label: thm:learningGamma
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:learningGamma-main} is $\delta$-PAC and terminates in at most (1+\omega)((L_{\nu}\log(1/\delta)+L_{\eta}\vcn{\theta}^2_2(d+\log(1/\delta)))\rho^*+(d+\log(1/\delta))(L_{\eta}\vcn{\theta}^2_2\rho_0+M)) pulls, ignoring both of the additive and multiplicative logarithms of $\Delta, \abr{\mc{W}}, \rho^*, \rho_0, M$

results.notes: Restated as Theorem K.2 in the appendix. Logarithmic factors ignored, hence O_tilde.

symbols.sigma_v: sigma^2 = v^T Sigma v with v = [theta, 1]: variance of the combined noise

source.label: thm:lower_bnd
source.quote: Assume $\Gamma$ is known, $\theta$ is unknown, and the noise process is jointly Gaussian ... For $\delta \in (0, 0.05]$, if the non-adaptive oracle algorithm acquires $T\leq \sigma^2\rho^{\ast}\log(1/\delta)/2$ samples on the problem instance where $\sigma^2:=v^{\top}\Sigma v$ and $v:=\begin{bmatrix}\theta & 1\end{bmatrix}$, then $\mathbb{P}(\widehat{w}\neq w^{\ast})\geq \delta$.

results.notes: Lower bound only for a specific non-adaptive oracle algorithm; holds for every instance. Paper notes it is likely not tight.

conditions: non-adaptive oracle algorithm that knows Gamma and uses the oracle IV estimator
there exists an instance (theta proportional to all-ones, Sigma_theta = 11^T) with noise satisfying Assumption 1

source.label: cor:lower_bnd
source.quote: There exists a problem instance ... with a noise process satisfying Assumption~\ref{assump:noise} such that if the non-adaptive oracle algorithm acquires $T\leq \max\{d\|\theta\|_2^2, \sqrt{d}\|\theta\|_2\}\rho^{\ast}\log(1/\delta)/2$ samples, then $\mathbb{P}(\widehat{w}\neq w^{\ast})\geq \delta$ for $\delta\in (0, 0.05]$.

results.notes: Existence-of-instance lower bound for the non-adaptive oracle algorithm.

conditions: offline data collected non-adaptively via fixed design xi

source.quote: Suppose that we have $\widehat{\Gamma}$ that is an OLS estimate from an offline dataset ... Algorithm \ref{alg-pluginHatGamma} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, a $6\gamma$-good arm is returned ... Also, the algorithm terminates in at most c(1+\omega)L_{\nu}\log(1/\delta)\rho^{\ast}(\gamma)+c(1+\omega)^2L_{\nu}\log(1/\delta)\fr{\sigma_\eta^2\overline{\log}(Z_{T},\delta)}{\sigma_{\min}(A(\xi, \Gamma))}\fr{\rho(\xi,\gamma)}{T}\vee cr(\omega) samples

results.notes: c hides logs of Delta, |W|, gamma. Statement's 'vee' placement ambiguous; recorded as max of sum and r(omega). Objective is approximate (6 gamma-good arm).
